general.title: Getting started
general.summary: Sign in, add NEXORIA to a server and open its dashboard.

sections.heading: Sign in
sections.body: Use Log in with Discord on the home page. NEXORIA only reads your basic profile and the list of servers you are in so it can show the servers you can manage.

sections.heading: Add the bot
sections.body: Open Servers, choose a server you own or administrate and press Begin setup (or Invite Bot). After the bot joins, the server shows Manage Server.

sections.heading: Open the dashboard
sections.body: Press Manage Server. Everything for that server is split into modules in the left sidebar: General, Moderation, Support, Community and Integrations.

general.title: Dashboard access & roles
general.summary: Who can open and edit a server's dashboard.

sections.heading: Owner and co-owners
sections.body: The server owner and configured co-owners can use every module and can decide who else may use the dashboard in Manage Servers > General Settings.

sections.heading: Administrators
sections.body: A Discord administrator only gets dashboard access after the owner allows it in General Settings. Servers you cannot manage are hidden from the server switcher; the full server list shows them as No access.

sections.heading: Member lists
sections.body: Whenever the dashboard lists members (for example in Owner control) they are sorted from the highest-ranked role in the server down to the lowest.

sections.heading: Notifications
sections.body: Choose which direct messages NEXORIA may send you, for example moderation warnings and ticket-report block notices.

sections.heading: Security and restrictions
sections.body: Shows the sign-in sessions on your account and any block that stops you from reporting tickets, either in one server or globally.

sections.heading: Connected accounts
sections.body: Link Roblox and other accounts. Linked accounts are used by Roblox Verification and anti-alt protection.

general.title: Ticket reports, files and transcripts
general.summary: How reported tickets, stored files and downloaded transcripts work.

sections.heading: Reported tickets
sections.body: A reported ticket shows its status (Unresolved, Ongoing, Resolved or Denied) next to the report button and a global case ID such as TKT-000001 so staff and admins can find it quickly.

sections.heading: Stored images and files
sections.body: Images and files from tickets are processed by the host: images are converted to text and compressed into a ZIP, files are kept inside ZIPs and are never executed. They are rebuilt only when someone opens or downloads them.

sections.heading: Transcript downloads
sections.body: A downloaded transcript is a standalone file. Each image and file link contains a single-use download token (255 characters, valid for 3 days). After it is used or expires the link stops working. Administrators can revoke tokens from the Admin panel.

general.title: Server switcher
general.summary: Switch between the servers you manage without leaving the dashboard.

sections.heading: Who appears
sections.body: Only servers where NEXORIA is installed AND where you are allowed to use the dashboard (owner, co-owner or an administrator the owner approved). Servers you cannot edit are not offered, and opening one from View All Servers shows Dashboard access required.

sections.heading: Unsaved changes
sections.body: If a page has unsaved changes you are asked before switching.

general.title: Roles: hierarchy and colours
general.summary: Which roles you may grant and how names are coloured.

sections.heading: Granting roles
sections.body: Anywhere the dashboard gives roles to people (Roblox gamepass and group binds, reaction roles, join roles, the mute role, custom command role actions) you can only choose roles below your own highest role. Owners and co-owners can choose any role.

sections.heading: Colours
sections.body: A member's name uses the colour of their highest role that has a colour, exactly like Discord. Roles use their own colour. Member lists are sorted from the highest-ranked role to the lowest.

general.title: Admin panel
general.summary: Sign-in, ticket review reports, blocked users and transcript downloads.

sections.heading: Signing in
sections.body: Enter the admin username and password. Your Discord account must also be granted admin access. Failed attempts are rate limited.

sections.heading: Reported reviews
sections.body: Every report has a global case ID (RVW-000001 style) and a status: Unresolved, Ongoing or Resolved. Filter by status or search by case ID. You can block the reviewer in one server or on every server.

sections.heading: Blocked users
sections.body: Security & restrictions lists everyone blocked from reviewing or reporting, per server or global, with an Unblock button.

sections.heading: Transcript downloads
sections.body: Shows who downloaded a transcript and which of its single-use tokens were used. Invalidate a whole download or one token at any time.

general.title: How the website finds the bot

sections.heading: The one URL that matters
sections.body: The published config.json only needs LOCAL_BOT_URL (the current Cloudflare tunnel) and an UPDATED_AT time. Old multi-host fields are removed automatically.

sections.heading: If the site says the bridge is waiting
sections.body: The website reads the published copy of config.json, not the local file. Check that start-tunnel.ps1 printed [GitHub] SUCCESS, then reload the site.

general.title: How files are stored
general.summary: Images and files are kept inside ZIPs and rebuilt on demand.

sections.heading: No raw files
sections.body: Images (tickets, logging, moderation filters) become text inside a ZIP; every other file is stored inside a ZIP under a neutral name. Nothing on the host can run by accident.

sections.heading: No backups
sections.body: NEXORIA does not keep backup copies of data files any more; older .bak files and the Backups folder are deleted at startup to save space.

general.title: Advanced builder: full guide
general.summary: Everything on the Advanced command builder screen, button by button.

sections.heading: Opening it
sections.body: Dashboard > Custom Commands > New command > Advanced (or Edit on an existing command). The builder is a full-screen canvas with the node palette on the left, the canvas in the middle and a live preview on the right.

sections.heading: Adding and moving nodes
sections.body: Click a node in the palette to drop it on the canvas, or drag one out. New nodes never land on top of another node; if the spot is taken the node is moved to the nearest free space. You can still drag nodes on top of each other yourself. Drag a node from anywhere that is not a text box or button.

sections.heading: Connecting nodes
sections.body: Drag from an output port (right side) to an input port (left side). While you drag, the wire glows and every input you can connect to lights up. Wires route around other nodes automatically. Hover any port to see whether it is an input, an output, or the True / False branch.

sections.heading: Selecting several nodes
sections.body: Ctrl + click (Cmd on Mac) to build a selection. A bar appears with Create template, Delete and Clear. Dragging one selected node moves all of them.

sections.heading: Templates
sections.body: Right-click a node (or use the selection bar) and choose Create template, give it a name and description. The Templates button lists yours and the built-in ones with a search box; press Use to paste. Right-click a template to delete it. Templates keep the advanced variables they use and recreate them if missing.

sections.heading: Variables button
sections.body: Opens the list of Advanced variables for this server. Use + New to add one. Click a variable to jump to the node that uses it. See Variables for how sharing between servers works.

sections.heading: Undo, Redo, Fit
sections.body: Undo and Redo step through your edits. Fit zooms the canvas so every node is visible. Panning and zooming never count as changes.

sections.heading: Saving and leaving
sections.body: Save command stores the command. Back or Exit asks what to do only when something really changed: Keep editing, Exit without saving, or Save. Opening the editor and looking around never triggers the question.

sections.heading: Chart nodes
sections.body: The Charts group has 13 nodes (Bar, Line, Area, Pie, Donut, Scatter, Gauge, Sparkline, Histogram, Radar, Leaderboard, Table, Progress). Each shows a live preview of its own data inside the node. Choose where the data comes from: typed values (hardcoded, optional labels), an advanced variable, or the wire from the previous node. Values look like 3, 7, 5 or Mon:3, Tue:7. When the command runs the chart is posted in the channel as a text chart and its text is passed on to the next node.

sections.heading: Preview and Ask docs
sections.body: Run in the preview panel simulates your command safely with a test message and test roles. Ask docs opens the docs assistant over the builder so you can ask about any node.

general.title: Variables: text, advanced and shared
general.summary: How placeholders, stored values and shared values work.

sections.heading: Text variables
sections.body: Words in curly braces such as {user.mention}, {user.name}, {server.name} or {channel.mention} work in any message or text field. They are replaced each time the command runs. The Variables list in this documentation shows every one.

sections.heading: Advanced variables
sections.body: Advanced variables are named values NEXORIA remembers (counters, flags, text). Create them in the builder (Variables > + New) or on the Custom Commands page. Read one with {name}. Change one with Set Variable, Increment Variable, Append Variable, Set Variable If or Delete Variable nodes.

sections.heading: Shared variables
sections.body: Sharing lets another server use your variable. On the owner server press Share on the variable and pick Read or Read + Write; a long token is shown once. On the other server press Connect and paste the token; a local variable is created that follows the original. Revoke by turning sharing off, which invalidates the token and breaks every connection. Only give the token to servers you trust.

sections.heading: Variables inside templates
sections.body: A template remembers which advanced variables its nodes use (with their value and description). Pasting the template creates any that do not exist yet, without touching ones that do.

general.title: Listeners guide
general.summary: Run flows when something happens in Discord.

sections.heading: What a listener is
sections.body: A listener is an Advanced flow that starts from a Discord event instead of a typed command. Create one on Custom Commands > Listeners.

sections.heading: Events
sections.body: Pick the event on the Listener Event node: message created, edited or deleted, bulk delete, member joined, left or updated, and more. Event Value nodes expose fields such as the message text or the author.

sections.heading: Good habits
sections.body: Add an If node early to ignore bots or channels you do not care about, and avoid listeners that send a message for every message (they can loop).

general.title: Roblox verification guide
general.summary: How members verify and how staff can verify them by hand.

sections.heading: Member commands
sections.body: Members can run /verify, ?verify or !verify. NEXORIA walks them through linking their Roblox account and then gives the roles that match their binds.

sections.heading: Binds
sections.body: A bind connects something on Roblox (a gamepass, a group rank, an item...) to a Discord role. You can only choose roles below your own highest role unless you are the server owner or a co-owner.

sections.heading: Editing, short names and order
sections.body: Every bind has an Edit button for all of its settings and an optional short name (up to 24 characters) shown in the list. Binds are checked from top to bottom and the order is the rank: the top bind is rank #1. Use the arrows to move a bind up or down.

sections.heading: Only allow 1 role in a group
sections.body: Turn this on for the binds that should be exclusive. All binds with it on form one group, and a member only keeps the role of the highest-ranked matching bind (the one nearest the top). Lower ones are not given, and are taken away if the member already has them. Example: VIP 3 above VIP 2 above VIP 1, all with the setting on, so someone who owns all three passes only gets the VIP 3 role.

sections.heading: Checked every time
sections.body: /verify, ?verify, !verify, the verify buttons and the website check live whether verification is on, every single time they are used. Switching the Roblox Verification module on in the sidebar also turns verification itself on.

sections.heading: Manual verification
sections.body: The server owner or a co-owner can run /manualverify with the Discord member and, optionally, their Roblox username. The member is verified for that server only; their global NEXORIA integrations are not changed.

sections.heading: If it says verification is off
sections.body: Check that the Roblox Verification module is switched on in the sidebar AND enabled on its own Settings tab. Both switches must be on.

general.title: Tickets guide
general.summary: Panels, claiming, reviews, reports, sharing and transcripts.

sections.heading: Panels and subjects
sections.body: Build the panel message and its subjects in Ticket Tool > Settings. Each subject can have its own staff roles, category, welcome text and DM behaviour.

sections.heading: Claiming and closing
sections.body: Staff claim a ticket to take it. Closing sends the member a DM with a link to open the ticket and review it.

sections.heading: Reviews are private
sections.body: A support review (0 to 10, in steps of 0.1; you can type 5,0 or 5.0) is private. Only the ticket owner (in My Tickets) and the NEXORIA admin panel can see it. Server owners and staff cannot read an individual review.

sections.heading: Reporting
sections.body: Every ticket has a Report ticket button (in the ticket list and on the ticket page). Each report is a case with a global ID such as TKT-000001 and a status (Unresolved, Ongoing, Resolved or Denied) shown next to the button.

sections.heading: Sharing
sections.body: Ticket sharing is off by default. Enable it on a ticket to get a link anyone can open read-only; Regenerate replaces the link and Disable sharing turns it off.

sections.heading: Transcripts and files
sections.body: Images and files are stored safely on the host. Download Transcript saves a standalone page; its images and files open through single-use links that expire after 3 days.

general.title: Honeypot guide
general.summary: How the honeypot channels and the kick message work.

sections.heading: Channels
sections.body: NEXORIA creates honeypot channels and spreads them through your category list so a bot that posts in every channel cannot skip them. Nobody should type in them.

sections.heading: What happens
sections.body: When a member types there, NEXORIA removes their recent messages, applies the punishment you chose and DMs them: why it happened, a button to recover their account, and an invite back to your server. Administrators are never punished and do not add to the kick count.

sections.heading: Statistics
sections.body: The Kicks button on a honeypot message shows how many people were removed in your server (per honeypot channel) and the global totals.

general.title: Setup: build and export
general.summary: Server builder, progress estimate and exporting a server layout.

sections.heading: Building
sections.body: The builder can create roles, categories, channels, the ticket panel and honeypots. It asks whether to also set up Roblox verification. If you choose to replace existing channels it deletes and renames them one by one and shows what is left.

sections.heading: Permissions
sections.body: The bot needs Manage Roles, Manage Channels and a role placed ABOVE the roles it must create or edit. If something fails the builder tells you which permission is missing instead of stopping silently.

sections.heading: Progress
sections.body: The estimated time counts down every second and is re-estimated from how long steps are really taking.

sections.heading: Export
sections.body: Export saves roles, channels, categories, permissions and the server icon (you choose which parts) but never messages, members or tokens.

general.title: Notifications and your data
general.summary: Which DMs NEXORIA can send and how to remove your saved docs conversations.

sections.heading: DM settings
sections.body: User Settings > Notifications lets you turn each kind of DM off (moderation warnings, ticket staff replies, review report updates, review restriction DMs, verification messages).

sections.heading: Docs conversations
sections.body: Conversations with the docs assistant are saved on the host for your Discord account. In User Settings > Data you can delete chosen conversations or all of them.

general.title: Status & uptime
general.summary: How host status, uptime and incidents are recorded.

sections.heading: Heartbeat
sections.body: The host writes a heartbeat once a minute. If the host stops without a clean shutdown, the gap is recorded as an incident the next time it starts.

sections.heading: Clean stops
sections.body: Stopping or restarting the host normally records a clean stop, so planned restarts are not reported as unplanned downtime.

general.title: Glossary: how things work
general.summary: Short explanations of the main ideas (nodes, variables, templates, reports...).

sections.heading: What are nodes?
sections.body: Nodes are the building blocks of an Advanced command or listener. Each node does one small job: send a message, check a role, wait, change a variable, ban a member...  You connect nodes with wires, from an output port (right side) to an input port (left side). When the command runs, NEXORIA starts at the Trigger and follows the wires from node to node.  - Open the Advanced builder: Custom Commands > New command > Advanced • Add nodes from the palette on the left, grouped by what they do • Hover a port to see what it does

sections.heading: Ports and wires
sections.body: A port is the small dot on the edge of a node. The dot on the left is the input, the dot(s) on the right are outputs.  Drag from an output port to an input port to make a wire. Branch nodes (the If nodes) have two outputs: True (green) and False (red). Select a wire and press Delete, or right-click it, to remove it.  Wires route around other nodes by themselves. While you drag a wire the possible inputs glow.

sections.heading: Trigger
sections.body: The Trigger node starts a command. It sets the command name, the word people type, whether it is a slash command and/or uses a prefix, and the command scope.  Every command needs exactly one Trigger. Listeners use a Listener Event node instead, which starts the flow when a Discord event happens (a message is deleted, a member joins...).

sections.heading: Listeners
sections.body: A listener is an Advanced flow that runs when something happens in Discord instead of when someone types a command. Examples: log deleted messages, welcome new members, react to edited messages.  Start it with a Listener Event node and pick the event. Use Event Value nodes to read details about the event (the message text, the author...).

sections.heading: Slash command or prefix?
sections.body: A slash command is typed as /name and Discord shows its description. A prefix command is typed as a prefix plus the name, for example ?hello.  Command scope on the Trigger node chooses which one works: Prefix only, Slash only, or both. Slash commands need a description (use the Description node).

sections.heading: Text variables like {user.mention}
sections.body: Text variables are placeholders you type inside any message or text field, written in curly braces, for example {user.mention} or {server.name}. When the command runs NEXORIA swaps each one for the real value.  They only live for that one run. Documentation > Variables lists every one. For values that must be remembered between runs use Advanced variables.

sections.heading: Advanced variables
sections.body: Advanced variables are values NEXORIA remembers between runs, for example a counter or a toggle. Create them from the Variables button in the builder (or Custom Commands > Advanced variables).  Use them as {name} in text fields, and change them with the Set Variable, Increment Variable, Append Variable and Delete Variable nodes. Each server has its own list.

sections.heading: Shared variables
sections.body: A shared variable lets two servers use the same value.  - In the server that owns the variable, turn on sharing and choose read-only or read + write. NEXORIA shows a share token once; copy it then. • In the other server choose Connect and paste the token. A local variable is created that points at the original. • Reading gives the owner's current value. Writing only works if you enabled write access. • Turn sharing off at any time to revoke the token and break every connection.  Only share a token with servers you trust.

sections.heading: Templates
sections.body: Templates save a group of nodes (with the variables they use) so you can paste them into any command.  - Ctrl + click nodes to select several, then press Create template, or right-click a node and choose Create template • Give it a name and description • Open Templates to search them, press Use to paste, or right-click one to delete it  Templates are stored on the host for your server. Pasting also creates any variables the template needs.

sections.heading: Selecting several nodes
sections.body: Hold Ctrl (Cmd on Mac) and click nodes to add or remove them from the selection. A bar appears with Create template, Delete and Clear. Dragging any selected node moves the whole selection.  Click empty canvas to clear the selection.

sections.heading: Branches (True / False)
sections.body: Branch nodes ask a yes/no question: does the member have a role, is the message long, is it after 22:00... They have two outputs. True runs when the answer is yes, False runs when it is no. Connect each output to the path that should run.  If an output has no wire the flow simply ends there.

sections.heading: Who can use a command
sections.body: The Permissions node controls who may run a command: everyone, administrators, or specific roles. Logic nodes like If Permission and If Has Role can also check inside the flow.  To stop a person using the bot at all, use the Security nodes (Block User / Allow User) or the Access Control node.

sections.heading: Built-in commands
sections.body: Built-in commands ship with NEXORIA (moderation, verification, dashboard...). Open the node view of one to see exactly how it runs; it is shown with the same node cards as the Advanced builder, read-only. To make your own variation build a new Advanced command.

sections.heading: Modules
sections.body: NEXORIA is split into modules you can turn on and off per server: Moderation, Logging, Honeypot, Roblox Verification, Ticket Tool, Custom Commands, Member Automation, Reaction Roles, Webhooks and Setup. Each has its own page in the dashboard sidebar and its own documentation page.

sections.heading: Dashboard access
sections.body: The server owner and co-owners (chosen on the website under General Settings) can always use the dashboard. An administrator gets access only after the owner allows it. The server switcher only lists servers you are allowed to open.  Co-owners may also pick roles above their own, which normal administrators cannot.

sections.heading: Which roles can I assign?
sections.body: Wherever the dashboard gives roles to people (Roblox gamepass/group binds, reaction roles, join roles, the mute role, custom command role actions) you can only choose roles BELOW your own highest role. The server owner and co-owners can choose any role.  Roles above yours are greyed out, and the host refuses the save if one gets through.

sections.heading: How do tickets work?
sections.body: Members press a button on the ticket panel and NEXORIA opens a private channel for them and the staff. Staff can claim, add people, close, and share a ticket. When a ticket closes the member can review the support they got (0-10).  Images and files sent in a ticket are stored on the host (images as text inside a ZIP, files inside ZIPs). Members can download a transcript; its image/file links are single-use and expire after 3 days.

sections.heading: Ticket reports
sections.body: Every ticket has a Report button. A report gets a global case ID (TKT-000001 style) and a status: Unresolved, Ongoing, Resolved or Denied. The status is shown next to the button so everyone can see what happened.  Administrators work the reports in the Admin panel: filter by status, search by case ID, and change the status (the reporter gets a DM). Older review reports can also be blocked per server or globally.

sections.heading: What is in a transcript?
sections.body: A transcript is a standalone HTML copy of a ticket. Text is inside the file. Images and files load from the NEXORIA host through links with a single-use token (255 characters, valid for 3 days). Click an image to preview and zoom, or download it.  Each link works once; download the transcript again for fresh links. Administrators can see who downloaded a transcript and invalidate tokens.

sections.heading: Honeypot
sections.body: A honeypot is a channel no real member should ever type in. Hacked accounts that spam every channel type there, and NEXORIA then removes them (kick/softban, timeout or ban as you choose) and deletes their recent messages. The member gets a DM explaining what happened and how to recover the account.  Administrators are never punished and their messages do not count toward the kick statistics.

sections.heading: How does Roblox verification work?
sections.body: Members link their Roblox account and receive roles for it. They can start with /verify, ?verify or !verify.  Roles can be tied to gamepasses, groups and other Roblox conditions (binds). The server owner or a co-owner can verify someone by hand with /manualverify (pick the Discord member and optionally type their Roblox username). Manual verification only counts in that server.

sections.heading: Moderation module
sections.body: Moderation records every warn, mute, kick and ban as a case. Warning thresholds can run actions automatically (Log, Mute, Kick, Ban) when a member reaches a number of active warns.  Image filters block a specific image: upload it once and NEXORIA compares every image people post against it. A filter can combine actions (Log, Warn, Mute, Kick, Ban, Delete message).

sections.heading: Server builder and export
sections.body: Setup can build a ready-made server layout (roles, categories, channels, ticket panel, honeypots, optional Roblox verification) and can export your current server's structure (roles, channels, permissions, icon) without any messages, so you can rebuild it elsewhere.  The builder shows a live progress estimate and always asks before deleting or renaming anything.

sections.heading: Logging module
sections.body: Logging writes server events (message edits and deletes, joins, leaves, role changes...) to channels you choose. Attachments from logged messages are stored safely inside ZIPs on the host and never as normal files.

sections.heading: Chart nodes
sections.body: Chart nodes draw your numbers. Pick Bar, Line, Area, Pie, Donut, Scatter, Gauge, Sparkline, Histogram, Radar, Leaderboard, Table or Progress.  Each node shows a live preview inside the builder. The data can be:  - typed in (values like `3, 7, 5` or `Mon:3, Tue:7`, optional labels) • read from an advanced variable • taken from the wire, from the node before it  When the command runs the chart is posted as a text chart in the channel and also passed to the next node.

sections.heading: Verification binds: rank and 1 role only
sections.body: Each Roblox bind has a short name, an Edit button, and a rank (its position in the list, top = #1).  Turn on Only allow 1 role in a group for the binds that must be exclusive. All binds with it on act as one group: the member gets only the role of the highest-ranked matching bind, and lower ones are not given (or are removed).

sections.heading: The docs assistant
sections.body: This window answers from the documentation only, there is no AI service or API key involved. Ask about a node, a variable, or a module.  Drag the title bar to move it, drag any edge to resize it, then press Save to remember the position. The conversation list on the left keeps your chats on the host; the three-dot menu downloads or deletes them.

modules.title: Custom Commands
modules.summary: Build prefix and slash commands with a visual node graph, branching conditions, roles, variables, Discord actions, a simulator, and execution controls. Basic mode is for simple responses; Advanced mode is a connected node editor for complete command logic.

sections.heading: Basic mode — quick commands
sections.body: Basic mode is for a straightforward trigger → response command. Choose Prefix or Slash, enter the trigger, add the response, choose who can run it, then save. Use Basic when the command only needs a small number of ordered actions and no visual branching.

sections.heading: Advanced mode — visual command flows
sections.body: Advanced mode opens an empty canvas for a new command. Add exactly one Trigger node, then connect its output to the first executable node. Nothing is inserted automatically. Existing commands are migrated into their graph without changing their saved behavior.

sections.heading: Every Advanced node
sections.body: Trigger — required entry node; sets command name, trigger, Prefix/Slash mode, scope, prefix, and slash description. Description — stores a separate slash-command description. Permissions — controls Everyone, Administrators, or selected roles. Send Message — sends plain Discord text with variables. Send Embed — sends a title/description/color embed. Reply — replies to the triggering message. Mention User — sends the command user's mention plus optional text. Add Role — adds a selected role to the user. Remove Role — removes a selected role. React — adds a reaction to the triggering message. DM User — sends the command user a direct message. Delete Trigger — deletes the prefix message that invoked the command. Wait — pauses execution for the selected delay. Stop — ends the flow immediately. If — flexible Target → Condition → Value/Role branching node. If Contains — checks trigger text for a substring. If Has Role — checks whether the user has a selected role. Random Chance — randomly chooses the True branch using a percentage. Comment — builder-only documentation note. Set Variable — creates or overwrites a temporary command variable. Change Variable — adds or subtracts a number from a variable. Log — writes a diagnostic message to the bot console.

sections.heading: Command nodes
sections.body: Trigger is required and defines the command name, trigger text, prefix/slash mode, scope, and slash description. Description stores a slash-command description when you want metadata separate from Trigger. Permissions controls Everyone, Administrators, or selected roles. These metadata nodes configure the command and are not sent to Discord as actions.

sections.heading: Discord action nodes
sections.body: Send Message sends normal text and supports documented variables. Send Embed creates a title, description, and color. Reply replies to the triggering message. Mention User adds the command user's mention. Add Role and Remove Role change a member's roles when the bot can manage the target role. React reacts to the triggering message. DM User sends a direct message. Delete Trigger removes the triggering prefix message when Discord permissions allow it.

sections.heading: Flow nodes
sections.body: Wait pauses execution for a controlled number of milliseconds. Stop ends execution immediately. Connect output ports directly to input ports; a normal input accepts one incoming connection. Wires move with nodes and can be selected and removed from the custom editor menu.

sections.heading: Logic and condition nodes
sections.body: If is the flexible condition node. Choose a Target such as User, Message, Channel, Command, or Variable, then choose the matching condition and value/role. User supports Has Role, Doesn't Have Role, Is Administrator, and Is Server Owner. Message supports Contains, Doesn't Contain, Equals, and Doesn't Equal. Channel can check text, thread, and forum types. Command can compare name or trigger. Variable compares a stored command variable. Random Chance branches by percentage. Branch nodes expose separate True and False outputs.

sections.heading: Variable nodes and custom variables
sections.body: Set Variable creates or overwrites a temporary command variable. Change Variable adds or subtracts a numeric amount. Custom variables can also be created in the command editor, edited, inserted into supported message fields, and deleted. Use {var.name} for custom command variables and the documented built-in variable names such as {user.mention}, {server.name}, {channel.name}, and {command.name}.

sections.heading: Utility nodes
sections.body: Log writes a diagnostic line to the bot console and is useful while debugging a flow. Comment is a builder-only note and never sends a Discord message. Use comments to explain why a branch or variable exists.

sections.heading: Preview, validation, and console
sections.body: Run opens the custom preview. It simulates a user invoking the command, shows bot replies as a conversation, evaluates branches, and records diagnostics. Preview runs do not change Discord. Nodes with missing required data receive a red problem outline. The console stays available between preview runs until Clear console is pressed.

sections.heading: Editing and navigation
sections.body: Drag a node header to move it. Drag directly from an output port to an input port to create a wire. Right-click inside the builder opens only the NEXORIA editor menu with relevant actions such as Duplicate, Center, Delete, Remove connection, and Add node here. Back and Exit both respect unsaved changes and ask before leaving. Use Cancel/Back to leave the editor without accidentally navigating outside the command workflow.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.body: Role gate: Trigger /staff → If (User → Has Role → Staff) → True → Add Role/Send Message; False → Send Message. Variable counter: Trigger ?count → Set Variable count=1 → Change Variable count +1 → Send Message "Count: {count}". Conditional text: Trigger ?hello → If (Message → Contains → hello) → True → Reply "Hello!"; False → Reply "Try saying hello.".

sections.heading: Built-in commands
sections.body: NEXORIA built-in commands are always available and cannot be disabled or deleted. Current built-ins are /dashboard, /help, /discord, /status, /verify, /unverify, /mute, and /unmute. Built-in commands are shown first; custom commands are listed after the built-in category.

sections.heading: Scope nodes — typed outputs
sections.body: Scope Input is a reusable typed output node. Choose Text, Full Trigger Message, Rest of Message, Command Argument, Quoted Text, Number, Boolean, URL, Emoji, Command User Mention, First User Mention in Message, User ID, User Name, Role Mention/ID, Channel Mention/ID, Trigger Text, Command Name, Server Name/ID, or time values. Argument and quoted scopes can choose an argument number. Every scope node has a stable node ID token such as {scope-node-id}. Connect its value output to an action and insert the token into supported fields; NEXORIA resolves it at execution time. Example: Trigger → Scope Input (Command Argument #1) → Send Message with `You entered {scope-node-id}`. Multiple scope outputs can feed different nodes, and one output can be referenced by multiple downstream fields.

sections.heading: Templates
sections.body: The Advanced builder includes reusable templates. Starter templates provide common patterns such as a welcome message, argument responder, and role gate. Save any graph as a named template with a description, then use it to create a new graph. Templates are stored for the server and reset command metadata such as the Trigger name so the same graph can be reused safely.

sections.heading: Advanced variable usage and locations
sections.body: The Advanced Variables manager shows each variable's current value, permissions, known node locations, and shared-server consumers. Click a variable to inspect every command/node that references it. Select a location to open that command and focus the exact node. Inside the Advanced builder, the Variables panel provides the same navigation. Shared variables continue to respect read/write exposure permissions; a connection without the required permission is treated as a node problem.

sections.heading: Output chaining
sections.body: Output nodes are first-class values. Connect a Scope Input or another output-producing node into a transform, condition, or action. Each output node has a stable token such as {node-id}. Message, embed, DM, log, variable, and compatible condition fields can resolve those tokens. One output can feed multiple downstream nodes, allowing a single captured value to be reused throughout a command.

sections.heading: Roles you can grant
sections.body: When you pick a role that NEXORIA will give to people, you can only choose roles below your own highest role. The server owner and co-owners (set on the website under General Settings) can choose any role. Roles above your own are greyed out in the list, and the host rejects the save if one slips through.

sections.heading: Builder: moving nodes
sections.body: Press and drag a node from anywhere that is not a text box, dropdown or button: the title bar, labels or empty space all work. Text is never selected while you drag.

sections.heading: Builder: wires
sections.body: Wires follow a smooth curve when nothing is in the way and automatically route around other nodes when something is. Drag from an output port to an input port to connect; select a wire and press Delete to remove it.

sections.heading: Builder: leaving the editor
sections.body: Back and Exit ask first when there are unsaved changes: Keep editing, Exit without saving, or Save. Closing the editor with Escape or by clicking outside asks the same question.

sections.heading: Categories
sections.body: Categories are only for organising. They appear as a tree; the toggle on each row enables or disables every command in it at once.

modules.title: Nexoria Honeypot
modules.summary: Create visible trap channels that delete messages, apply a configurable punishment, optionally DM the user with a server invite, and record every trigger.

sections.heading: Honeypot channels
sections.body: Create multiple Honeypot text channels directly from the dashboard. NEXORIA places each new channel at a random position and tracks it by Discord channel ID, so renaming the channel does not break the trap. If the channel is deleted in Discord, it is removed from the dashboard automatically.

sections.heading: Punishments
sections.body: Choose Softban (Kick), Timeout, Ban, or Log Only. Timeout and temporary Ban durations are configurable. The triggered message is deleted before the configured action is applied. Server owners and administrators are protected from automatic punishment.

sections.heading: Trigger message
sections.body: Each Honeypot channel receives a NEXORIA-branded warning message with the current punishment and a live trigger count. The message includes NEXORIA Dashboard, NEXORIA Documentation, Invite NEXORIA, and a Kicks button showing the number of triggers in that channel.

sections.heading: DM on trigger
sections.body: Optionally DM a triggered user with a NEXORIA-branded notice and an invite back to the server. Administrator example text is only included for administrator previews; administrators themselves are protected from automatic punishment.

sections.heading: Logging
sections.body: Honeypot Triggered is a normal Logging event. The Honeypot module can set its log channel directly, and that same channel is synchronized with Logging → Honeypot Triggered. If no Discord log channel is selected, the event can still be retained in the Logging history.

sections.heading: Punishment
sections.body: Punishment is a multi-select. When more than one is chosen the strongest applies: Ban over Kick over Timeout over Log.

modules.title: Logging
modules.summary: Server activity logging — pick a channel per log type (or per whole category), self-posted or via webhook, with ignore lists for noisy channels/roles/users.

sections.heading: Log types
sections.body: Grouped into categories (Bot, Custom Commands, Applications, Channels, Roles, Members, Messages, Voice, and more) — expand a category to set a channel for each type inside it individually, or set the whole category at once. Custom Command Used records custom command execution with the user, channel, and command name.

sections.heading: Self-post vs. webhook
sections.body: By default NEXORIA posts log messages itself. A channel can instead be set to use a webhook — useful for custom branding in that channel — but since anyone who obtains the webhook URL can post to it, this is opt-in per channel with a warning before you turn it on.

sections.heading: Ignore lists
sections.body: Channels, roles, and users can be excluded from logging entirely, so noisy bots or a specific channel don't flood your log channels.

sections.heading: Attachments
sections.body: Attachments from logged messages are never saved as normal files. Images are converted to text inside a ZIP and every other file (for example .bat or .cpp) is stored inside a ZIP, then rebuilt only when someone opens or downloads it. Risky file types download inside a ZIP.

modules.title: Member Automation
modules.summary: Gateway, Welcomer and Leaver automation in one module.

sections.heading: Gateway & Welcomer
sections.body: Automatically assign a configured join role and send a customizable welcome message.

sections.heading: Leaver
sections.body: Send a customizable goodbye message with member ping and remaining member count.

sections.heading: Join and bot roles
sections.body: When you pick a role that NEXORIA will give to people, you can only choose roles below your own highest role. The server owner and co-owners (set on the website under General Settings) can choose any role. Roles above your own are greyed out in the list, and the host rejects the save if one slips through.

modules.title: Moderation
modules.summary: Warnings, mutes, kicks, bans and permanent moderation case history.

sections.heading: Commands
sections.body: NEXORIA provides /mute, /unmute, /ban, /unban, /kick, /warn, /unwarn, /list and /case. Commands are enabled by default while the module itself can be disabled per server.

sections.heading: Warnings
sections.body: Warnings stack by user. /list shows active and historical warns, including when and why each warning was created. /unwarn closes the most recent active warning without deleting its history.

sections.heading: Cases
sections.body: Every moderation action receives a server CASE ID and a global NEX ID. Case IDs can be opened from Discord through the linked NEXORIA website case page.

sections.heading: Warning thresholds
sections.body: Server owners and configured co-owners can configure actions that trigger when a member reaches a selected active warning count or higher.

sections.heading: Moderation emoji
sections.body: Choose a server emoji (or paste any emoji) in Settings > Moderation emoji. It is shown next to Moderation in the dashboard sidebar, the same way the other modules work.

sections.heading: Image filters
sections.body: Upload an image to block it. The host stores the file locally and compares the SHA-256 hash of every image sent in your server with it, so only the exact same file matches. Each filter can run any combination of: Log, Warn, Mute, Kick, Ban and Delete message. A ban replaces kick/mute; a kick replaces mute.

sections.heading: Warning threshold actions
sections.body: Warning rules can also run several actions at once (Log, Mute, Kick, Ban). Undoing a change returns the editor to its saved state and hides the Changes detected bar automatically.

modules.title: Reaction Roles
modules.summary: Send editable role-selection messages using reactions, buttons, or dropdowns.

sections.heading: Messages
sections.body: Create and edit messages after sending. NEXORIA keeps the message ID so changes update the existing Discord message.

sections.heading: Selection types
sections.body: Reactions support up to 20 role reactions. Buttons support up to 5 buttons. Dropdowns support up to 25 options.

sections.heading: Cooldowns
sections.body: A per-user message cooldown prevents rapid role switching.

sections.heading: Roles you can grant
sections.body: When you pick a role that NEXORIA will give to people, you can only choose roles below your own highest role. The server owner and co-owners (set on the website under General Settings) can choose any role. Roles above your own are greyed out in the list, and the host rejects the save if one slips through.

modules.title: Server Setup
modules.summary: Configure a complete server baseline, copy a server structure, or import selected server settings.

sections.heading: Setup modes
sections.body: Full Server, roles, channels, permissions, logging and status can be applied independently.

sections.heading: Server Copy Board
sections.body: Export a structure-only NEXORIA snapshot containing server settings, roles, role permissions and hierarchy, channels, categories, channel permission overwrites, optional emojis/stickers, and NEXORIA module settings. Messages, ticket transcripts and logging history are never exported.

sections.heading: Import
sections.body: Paste a snapshot, load a JSON file, or paste it from the clipboard. You can choose whether to remove existing roles, channels, or expressions before importing, and can independently enable server settings and NEXORIA module settings. Role and channel IDs are remapped automatically so logging and module references continue to point at the imported structure.

sections.heading: Discord limitations
sections.body: Managed bot/integration roles and Discord-managed resources cannot be deleted or recreated by a bot and are therefore skipped. Discord permissions and any settings the bot lacks permission to change are applied on a best-effort basis.

sections.heading: Terminal announcements
sections.body: Turn announcement publishing off if you do not want announcements from the bot owner posted in this server.

modules.title: Ticket Tool
modules.summary: Support tickets: panels users click to open a ticket, per-subject settings, staff claiming, closing DMs, share links, and insights.

sections.heading: Panels
sections.body: A panel is a message (plain text and/or an embed) with buttons or a dropdown that users click to open a ticket. Each option on a panel connects to a Ticket Template (a "subject"), so one panel can offer several kinds of tickets at once.

sections.heading: Subjects (Ticket Templates)
sections.body: Each subject has its own welcome message, close message, staff roles, user/staff/claimer channel permissions, ticket limits, creation cooldowns, an optional auto-close timer, and its own logging toggles.

sections.heading: Claiming & Staff-Only Claim
sections.body: Staff can claim a ticket to signal they're handling it. When Staff-Only Claim is on, only members with a staff role for that subject can claim.

sections.heading: Closing DM
sections.body: A guild-wide, customizable embed DM sent to whoever opened a ticket once it's closed, separate from a subject's own plain-text close message. Supports {ticket.url} — a link back to the person's own authenticated ticket page.

sections.heading: Share Links
sections.body: When sharing is turned on, a closed ticket can be given a public, read-only share link so its transcript can be sent to someone without dashboard access.

sections.heading: Insights
sections.body: Ticket volume, close rate, and staff performance over a selectable time period, computed from real ticket data — nothing here is simulated.

sections.heading: Reported reviews: status and case IDs
sections.body: When a review is reported, its report button shows the status (Unresolved, Ongoing or Resolved) and a global case ID such as RVW-000012. Administrators can filter by status and search by case ID in the Admin panel.

sections.heading: Blocking reviewers
sections.body: Administrators can block a user from reviewing tickets in one server or on every server. The user gets a DM unless they turned off Review restriction DMs in User Settings > Notifications. Everyone who is blocked is listed under Admin panel > Security & restrictions > Blocked users.

sections.heading: Images, files and transcripts
sections.body: Ticket images are converted to text and stored inside ZIP files; other files are stored inside ZIPs under a neutral name, so nothing on the host can run by accident. They are rebuilt only when opened or downloaded. Click an image to preview and zoom, or use Download. Downloaded transcripts load images and files through single-use tokens (255 characters, valid 3 days).

sections.heading: Transcript download tokens (admins)
sections.body: Admin panel > Tickets > Transcript downloads, and each ticket's detail view, show who downloaded a transcript, when, and which tokens were used. Invalidate a whole download or a single token at any time.

modules.title: Roblox Verification
modules.summary: Official NEXORIA Roblox verification for server members.

sections.heading: How verification works
sections.body: Members use /verify in a server, choose the Roblox account connected to their NEXORIA identity, confirm the account, and complete verification. NEXORIA then applies the server's verification state and can remove the Unverified role.

sections.heading: Roblox Verification channel
sections.body: When verification is enabled, NEXORIA creates or uses the configured verification channel, posts its official verification information there, and opens a dedicated thread where members can use /verify.

sections.heading: Official message
sections.body: The official verification message is controlled by NEXORIA and cannot be edited from the dashboard. This keeps the message consistent and clearly identifies it as an official NEXORIA message.

sections.heading: Privacy
sections.body: Members can manage whether their Roblox username is shared with the server from the verification privacy controls.

sections.heading: Roles you can grant
sections.body: When you pick a role that NEXORIA will give to people, you can only choose roles below your own highest role. The server owner and co-owners (set on the website under General Settings) can choose any role. Roles above your own are greyed out in the list, and the host rejects the save if one slips through.

sections.heading: Colours
sections.body: Role names in lists use the role's colour.

modules.title: Webhooks
modules.summary: Create, customize and execute Discord webhooks.

sections.heading: Webhook control
sections.body: Create webhooks in text channels, change their names and avatars, choose channels, and send rich messages with embeds and mention controls.

faq.title: What are nodes?
faq.answer:
Nodes are the building blocks of an Advanced command or listener. Each node does one small job: send a message, check a role, wait, change a variable, ban a member...

You connect nodes with wires, from an output port (right side) to an input port (left side). When the command runs, NEXORIA starts at the Trigger and follows the wires from node to node.

- Open the Advanced builder: Custom Commands > New command > Advanced
- Add nodes from the palette on the left, grouped by what they do
- Hover a port to see what it does

faq.title: Ports and wires
faq.answer:
A port is the small dot on the edge of a node. The dot on the left is the input, the dot(s) on the right are outputs.

Drag from an output port to an input port to make a wire. Branch nodes (the If nodes) have two outputs: True (green) and False (red). Select a wire and press Delete, or right-click it, to remove it.

Wires route around other nodes by themselves. While you drag a wire the possible inputs glow.

faq.title: Trigger
faq.answer:
The Trigger node starts a command. It sets the command name, the word people type, whether it is a slash command and/or uses a prefix, and the command scope.

Every command needs exactly one Trigger. Listeners use a Listener Event node instead, which starts the flow when a Discord event happens (a message is deleted, a member joins...).

faq.title: Listeners
faq.answer:
A listener is an Advanced flow that runs when something happens in Discord instead of when someone types a command. Examples: log deleted messages, welcome new members, react to edited messages.

Start it with a Listener Event node and pick the event. Use Event Value nodes to read details about the event (the message text, the author...).

faq.title: Slash command or prefix?
faq.answer:
A slash command is typed as /name and Discord shows its description. A prefix command is typed as a prefix plus the name, for example ?hello.

Command scope on the Trigger node chooses which one works: Prefix only, Slash only, or both. Slash commands need a description (use the Description node).

faq.title: Text variables like {user.mention}
faq.answer:
Text variables are placeholders you type inside any message or text field, written in curly braces, for example {user.mention} or {server.name}. When the command runs NEXORIA swaps each one for the real value.

They only live for that one run. Documentation > Variables lists every one. For values that must be remembered between runs use Advanced variables.

faq.title: Advanced variables
faq.answer:
Advanced variables are values NEXORIA remembers between runs, for example a counter or a toggle. Create them from the Variables button in the builder (or Custom Commands > Advanced variables).

Use them as {name} in text fields, and change them with the Set Variable, Increment Variable, Append Variable and Delete Variable nodes. Each server has its own list.

faq.title: Shared variables
faq.answer:
A shared variable lets two servers use the same value.

- In the server that owns the variable, turn on sharing and choose read-only or read + write. NEXORIA shows a share token once; copy it then.
- In the other server choose Connect and paste the token. A local variable is created that points at the original.
- Reading gives the owner's current value. Writing only works if you enabled write access.
- Turn sharing off at any time to revoke the token and break every connection.

Only share a token with servers you trust.

faq.title: Templates
faq.answer:
Templates save a group of nodes (with the variables they use) so you can paste them into any command.

- Ctrl + click nodes to select several, then press Create template, or right-click a node and choose Create template
- Give it a name and description
- Open Templates to search them, press Use to paste, or right-click one to delete it

Templates are stored on the host for your server. Pasting also creates any variables the template needs.
related: How do I select several nodes?

faq.title: Selecting several nodes
faq.answer:
Hold Ctrl (Cmd on Mac) and click nodes to add or remove them from the selection. A bar appears with Create template, Delete and Clear. Dragging any selected node moves the whole selection.

Click empty canvas to clear the selection.

faq.title: Branches (True / False)
faq.answer:
Branch nodes ask a yes/no question: does the member have a role, is the message long, is it after 22:00... They have two outputs. True runs when the answer is yes, False runs when it is no. Connect each output to the path that should run.

If an output has no wire the flow simply ends there.

faq.title: Who can use a command
faq.answer:
The Permissions node controls who may run a command: everyone, administrators, or specific roles. Logic nodes like If Permission and If Has Role can also check inside the flow.

To stop a person using the bot at all, use the Security nodes (Block User / Allow User) or the Access Control node.

faq.title: Built-in commands
faq.answer: Built-in commands ship with NEXORIA (moderation, verification, dashboard...). Open the node view of one to see exactly how it runs; it is shown with the same node cards as the Advanced builder, read-only. To make your own variation build a new Advanced command.

faq.title: Modules
faq.answer: NEXORIA is split into modules you can turn on and off per server: Moderation, Logging, Honeypot, Roblox Verification, Ticket Tool, Custom Commands, Member Automation, Reaction Roles, Webhooks and Setup. Each has its own page in the dashboard sidebar and its own documentation page.

faq.title: Dashboard access
faq.answer:
The server owner and co-owners (chosen on the website under General Settings) can always use the dashboard. An administrator gets access only after the owner allows it. The server switcher only lists servers you are allowed to open.

Co-owners may also pick roles above their own, which normal administrators cannot.

faq.title: Which roles can I assign?
faq.answer:
Wherever the dashboard gives roles to people (Roblox gamepass/group binds, reaction roles, join roles, the mute role, custom command role actions) you can only choose roles BELOW your own highest role. The server owner and co-owners can choose any role.

Roles above yours are greyed out, and the host refuses the save if one gets through.

faq.title: How do tickets work?
faq.answer:
Members press a button on the ticket panel and NEXORIA opens a private channel for them and the staff. Staff can claim, add people, close, and share a ticket. When a ticket closes the member can review the support they got (0-10).

Images and files sent in a ticket are stored on the host (images as text inside a ZIP, files inside ZIPs). Members can download a transcript; its image/file links are single-use and expire after 3 days.

faq.title: Ticket reports
faq.answer:
Every ticket has a Report button. A report gets a global case ID (TKT-000001 style) and a status: Unresolved, Ongoing, Resolved or Denied. The status is shown next to the button so everyone can see what happened.

Administrators work the reports in the Admin panel: filter by status, search by case ID, and change the status (the reporter gets a DM). Older review reports can also be blocked per server or globally.

faq.title: What is in a transcript?
faq.answer:
A transcript is a standalone HTML copy of a ticket. Text is inside the file. Images and files load from the NEXORIA host through links with a single-use token (255 characters, valid for 3 days). Click an image to preview and zoom, or download it.

Each link works once; download the transcript again for fresh links. Administrators can see who downloaded a transcript and invalidate tokens.

faq.title: Honeypot
faq.answer:
A honeypot is a channel no real member should ever type in. Hacked accounts that spam every channel type there, and NEXORIA then removes them (kick/softban, timeout or ban as you choose) and deletes their recent messages. The member gets a DM explaining what happened and how to recover the account.

Administrators are never punished and their messages do not count toward the kick statistics.

faq.title: How does Roblox verification work?
faq.answer:
Members link their Roblox account and receive roles for it. They can start with /verify, ?verify or !verify.

Roles can be tied to gamepasses, groups and other Roblox conditions (binds). The server owner or a co-owner can verify someone by hand with /manualverify (pick the Discord member and optionally type their Roblox username). Manual verification only counts in that server.

faq.title: Moderation module
faq.answer:
Moderation records every warn, mute, kick and ban as a case. Warning thresholds can run actions automatically (Log, Mute, Kick, Ban) when a member reaches a number of active warns.

Image filters block a specific image: upload it once and NEXORIA compares every image people post against it. A filter can combine actions (Log, Warn, Mute, Kick, Ban, Delete message).

faq.title: Server builder and export
faq.answer:
Setup can build a ready-made server layout (roles, categories, channels, ticket panel, honeypots, optional Roblox verification) and can export your current server's structure (roles, channels, permissions, icon) without any messages, so you can rebuild it elsewhere.

The builder shows a live progress estimate and always asks before deleting or renaming anything.

faq.title: Logging module
faq.answer: Logging writes server events (message edits and deletes, joins, leaves, role changes...) to channels you choose. Attachments from logged messages are stored safely inside ZIPs on the host and never as normal files.

faq.title: Chart nodes
faq.answer:
Chart nodes draw your numbers. Pick Bar, Line, Area, Pie, Donut, Scatter, Gauge, Sparkline, Histogram, Radar, Leaderboard, Table or Progress.

Each node shows a live preview inside the builder. The data can be:

- typed in (values like `3, 7, 5` or `Mon:3, Tue:7`, optional labels)
- read from an advanced variable
- taken from the wire, from the node before it

When the command runs the chart is posted as a text chart in the channel and also passed to the next node.

faq.title: Verification binds: rank and 1 role only
faq.answer:
Each Roblox bind has a short name, an Edit button, and a rank (its position in the list, top = #1).

Turn on Only allow 1 role in a group for the binds that must be exclusive. All binds with it on act as one group: the member gets only the role of the highest-ranked matching bind, and lower ones are not given (or are removed).

faq.title: The docs assistant
faq.answer:
This window answers from the documentation only, there is no AI service or API key involved. Ask about a node, a variable, or a module.

Drag the title bar to move it, drag any edge to resize it, then press Save to remember the position. The conversation list on the left keeps your chats on the host; the three-dot menu downloads or deletes them.

nodes.label: Bar Chart
nodes.help: Bar chart: one bar per value. Values can be typed in, read from a variable, or arrive on the wire. Optionally posts the chart to the channel.

nodes.label: Line Chart
nodes.help: Line chart: values joined by a line. Values can be typed in, read from a variable, or arrive on the wire. Optionally posts the chart to the channel.

nodes.label: Area Chart
nodes.help: Area chart: a line chart with the area filled in. Values can be typed in, read from a variable, or arrive on the wire. Optionally posts the chart to the channel.

nodes.label: Pie Chart
nodes.help: Pie chart: each value's share of the total. Values can be typed in, read from a variable, or arrive on the wire. Optionally posts the chart to the channel.

nodes.label: Donut Chart
nodes.help: Donut chart: a pie chart with a hole in the middle. Values can be typed in, read from a variable, or arrive on the wire. Optionally posts the chart to the channel.

nodes.label: Scatter Chart
nodes.help: Scatter plot: values as dots (use x:y pairs for exact positions). Values can be typed in, read from a variable, or arrive on the wire. Optionally posts the chart to the channel.

nodes.label: Gauge Chart
nodes.help: Gauge: one value shown against a maximum. Values can be typed in, read from a variable, or arrive on the wire. Optionally posts the chart to the channel.

nodes.label: Sparkline Chart
nodes.help: Sparkline: a tiny trend line with no axes. Values can be typed in, read from a variable, or arrive on the wire. Optionally posts the chart to the channel.

nodes.label: Histogram Chart
nodes.help: Histogram: how many values fall into each range (bins). Values can be typed in, read from a variable, or arrive on the wire. Optionally posts the chart to the channel.

nodes.label: Leaderboard Chart
nodes.help: Ranking: the highest values on top with medals for the first three. Values can be typed in, read from an advanced variable, or taken from the wire.

nodes.label: Table Chart
nodes.help: A simple two-column table of label and value. Values can be typed in, read from an advanced variable, or taken from the wire.

nodes.label: Progress Chart
nodes.help: Progress bars: each value as a percentage of the maximum (Gauge maximum). Values can be typed in, read from an advanced variable, or taken from the wire.

nodes.label: Radar Chart
nodes.help: Radar chart: one axis per label, great for comparing skills or stats. Values can be typed in, read from a variable, or arrive on the wire. Optionally posts the chart to the channel.

nodeGroupNotes.Command: Every command starts here. These nodes describe the command itself rather than doing work.
nodeGroupNotes.Listeners: Listeners react to Discord events instead of a typed command.
nodeGroupNotes.Inputs: Inputs turn something from the command (text, mentions, IDs...) into a value other nodes can use as {node-id}.
nodeGroupNotes.Discord: Actions that send messages or change things in your server.
nodeGroupNotes.Moderation: Actions against members and messages. The bot needs the matching Discord permission, and its role must be above the target.
nodeGroupNotes.Logic: Branch nodes have two outputs: True (green) and False (red). Connect each to the path that should run.
nodeGroupNotes.Transform: Text tools. Connect text in, use the result downstream.
nodeGroupNotes.Variables: Store values for later nodes in the same run.
nodeGroupNotes.Flow: Control the order, timing and stopping of a flow.
nodeGroupNotes.Outputs: Read values from the current run or publish a named output.
nodeGroupNotes.Charts: Charts turn numbers into a picture. In the builder every chart node shows a live preview of its own data. Data can be typed in, read from an advanced variable, or arrive on the wire from the node before it. When the command runs the chart is posted as a text chart (bars, lines, pies...) and its text is also passed on to the next node.
